newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol-Astra buy Argentine assets for $345 mln.
newsitem.headline: Repsol-Astra buy Argentine assets for $345 mln.

text.p: Spanish energy group Repsol said on Friday it would buy several stakes in Argentine refining and marketing firms, including a network of 700 service stations, in a deal worth $345 million via its subsidiary Astra.
Repsol has a 47.5 percent controlling stake in Astra.

The firm will buy stakes from Grupo Comercial del Plata, as follow: 32.5 percent in EG3, 42.5 percent in Refineria San Lorenzo (Refisan), 50 percent in Destilerias Argentina de Petroleo (Dapsa) and 50 percent in Parafinas del Plata.
It has also agreed to buy a separate 27.5 percent stake in EG3 from JME Inversiones.
After the deal, which is still being negotiated, Astra will become one of the main Argentinian oil companies and will increase its refining capacity to 3.2 million tonnes per year.
Astra will control 91.5 percent stake in the service station network, representing an around 15 percent market share in Argentina.

EG3 manufactures and retails fuels, asphalts, lubricants and compressed natural gas (CNG). It has a 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) capacity in Bahia Blanca and manages a network of 650 service stations.
The firm has sales of three million cubic metres of petrol products, 200 million cubic metres of CNG and 20,000 cubic metres of lubricants.
Refisan manufactures fuels and asphalt, has a refinery with output capacity for 37,000 bpd and a network of 30 service stations. Sales total 2 million cubic metres per year.
Dapsa also produces fuels and asphalts, as well as carrying out lubicants' blending. It has a 6,000 bpd refining capacity and 10 service stations.
Sales are around 300,000 tonnes of fuels, lubricants and asphalts.
Parafinas del Plata has sales of parafin and basic lubricant oils totalling around 50,000 tonnes per year.
